bull_case.point: Guidewire’s cloud migration is accelerating across the industry, with major insurers such as Zurich, Santam, Vaudoise, Sompo, and Germania already live on Guidewire Cloud, unlocking AI capabilities and expanding digital strategy.
The company delivered record ARR growth, with FY25 ARR surpassing $1 B and 19 cloud deals, including a 10‑year agreement with Liberty Mutual, exceeding consensus guidance.
Subscription revenue grew 33% YoY in Q4 2025, with subscription gross margins reaching 70%, underscoring the profitability of Guidewire’s cloud‑based subscription model.

Guidewire’s AI‑enabled capabilities, such as the ProNavigator assistant and new releases (Mammoth, Olos, Niseko, PricingCenter), are accelerating adoption and adding value to underwriting and claims workflows.
The P&C SaaS market totals $511.2 M across 12 vendors, indicating a sizable and growing addressable market for Guidewire’s core platform.
Guidewire remains the most visible core platform among P&C carriers, giving it a competitive moat in a fragmented market.

Recent company reports indicate strong sales growth and continued investment in manufacturing capacity, technology and customer-support capabilities. macro.narrative: The current macro backdrop, characterized by robust ISM manufacturing PMI, rising new orders, and a bullish equity environment, signals strong demand for technology solutions across the insurance sector. This expansion in end‑market demand, coupled with a long tilt in the computer & electronic products sector, directly supports Guidewire’s cloud‑based subscription model and AI‑enabled offerings. The upward‑sloping yield curve and low VIX suggest moderate financing costs, while the S&P’s position above its 20% bear level indicates favorable capital‑raising conditions for the company.

implications.why: Expansion in manufacturing and services new orders indicates insurers will invest in modernization, boosting demand for Guidewire’s cloud platform.
Higher demand and AI capabilities allow Guidewire to command premium subscription fees, strengthening pricing power.
Subscription ARR growth and 70% gross margin benefit from the macro expansion, improving margin sustainability.
While overall economic growth may raise labor costs, the subscription model limits direct input cost exposure.
Insurers’ increased capex for digital transformation supports Guidewire’s cloud migration deals and long‑term contracts.
An upward‑sloping yield curve raises borrowing rates, slightly increasing Guidewire’s financing costs.
